paragraphs: Sometimes mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud. Hyman identifies him as Rabbi Itai and says he is also sometimes called Rabbi Assi or Rabbi Yosi.

notes.text: The frozen text has Ami, whereas an earlier machine reading has Assi. That specific source variant remains unadjudicated from the scan. Hyman’s broader identifications are not authority merges.

Hyman (vol. III, p. 840) prints Rabbi Assi (ר׳ אסי), where the supplied Hebrew has Rabbi Ami (ר׳ אמי). The identifications with Rabbi Itai, Rabbi Assi and Rabbi Yosi are Hyman’s. This notice does not specify particular Yerushalmi passages for them.
